- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in subsequent periods; reduce forecast slope or add lagged mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile; apply slight upward bias to short-term forecasts.
- For 30-day forecasts, model shows persistent bias toward lower prices when sentiment is mixed (±0.33); apply upward adjustment of 0.5–1.5% to compensate.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.67 → -0.00 → +0.67), model tends to lag; add 1–2 days of lead time in forecast adjustment.
